narrative.overview: The homepage treats grailab as a working instrument placed on warm paper. The chart is the one machine on the desk: dark, precise, always the largest object in the room. Everything around it is paper, coffee ink, hairline rules and air. Linear contributes the discipline — aligned edges, a small number of scale steps, the product itself as the argument — while Notion contributes the material softness: a warm ground instead of white, gentle radii, and shadows that sit under objects rather than around them. The surface rejects the cold-fintech register (blue-black fields, neon data lines, glass cards), the marketing register of gradients and decorative illustrations, and the three-equal-cards template. The replay panel is the proof, so it appears before any feature list and actually runs.
keyCharacteristics: One dark instrument on a warm paper field.
Terracotta used as a sparse signal, never as a wash.
Self-hosted Schibsted Grotesk for Latin and figures; Noto Sans SC for Chinese.
16px surfaces, 1px hairlines, one soft offset shadow per elevated object.
Monochrome candles (hollow up, filled down) so direction never depends on hue.
Generous margins and short lines of copy.

rules.name: The One Instrument Rule
rules.body: Only the replay chart and the pane preview are dark. A second dark block on the page would compete with the product itself; the statement band uses coffee, not the chart ground.

rules.name: The Sparse Signal Rule
rules.body: Terracotta marks actions and live state, not surfaces. If a section reads as terracotta at arm's length, the rule has been broken.

rules.name: The Legible Fill Rule
rules.body: White text on terracotta is only legal on #AD5A3D or darker. #C46F50 carries graphics, rules and large marks, never small white type.

rules.name: The Tabular Data Rule
rules.body: Tabular figures belong to prices, clocks, counters and axes. The plan price stays proportional so it reads as one number rather than a slot machine.

rules.name: The Two-Script Rule
rules.body: Never set a Chinese headline in Schibsted's fallback; the CJK face must load before the hero paints. Latin display and Chinese body may mix on one line, but weights are chosen per script rather than inherited blindly.

rules.name: The Generous Margin Rule
rules.body: Whitespace is a material, not leftover space. A section earns separation with at least 72px of field; a divider is a refinement, never the only thing holding two sections apart.

rules.name: The Flat Hairline Rule
rules.body: Structure is a 1px rule at 12% ink. Elevation is a soft shadow with an offset and a blur. A hairline under a wide shadow is the ghost card and is forbidden.

dos: Do keep the chart the largest and darkest object on the first screen.
Do use #AD5A3D for white-on-terracotta small text and reserve #C46F50 for graphics and large marks.
Do label synthetic market data in the same viewport as the chart.
Do hold body copy to 34–46ch and let the page breathe at 72–118px section rhythm.
Do use hollow-up / filled-down candles so direction survives colour blindness and desaturation.
Do give every control a 44px target and a visible terracotta focus ring.
donts: Don't introduce a second accent hue for “buy” or “profit”; the chart is monochrome and the signal is terracotta.
Don't put a border and a wide shadow on the same surface.
Don't use gradients, glass, neon glows, or a cold blue-black fintech ground.
Don't turn features into equal icon-heading-text cards; the page uses figures and hairline rows.
Don't set a Chinese headline in a Latin face or vice versa; the two scripts have separate responsibilities.
Don't invent testimonials, customer logos, performance data or live prices.
